data.name: CaseBundle.Readme
data.value: SteamSentinel {0} This bundle contains records only. It includes no scanned files, quarantined samples or archive passwords, and is not uploaded automatically. scan.json is the pre-remediation scan, plan.json is the user-confirmed plan, and result.json records actual execution and verification. follow-up.json, when present, is a targeted follow-up, not a full-disk scan. batches.json, when present, records the original selection, excluded targets and all batch results. batches/ retains each batch's separate plan and execution record. content-follow-up.json inspects the original content scope; follow-up.json separately inspects the system and Steam. Neither replaces the other. trust-proxy-diagnostics.json, when present, is the latest local, read-only certificate and proxy collection. Use its recorded time. It does not overwrite the original scan or prove a complete rescan or successful remediation. related-components.json, when present, records sources, hosts, candidates and read-only follow-up rounds for the current component association inspection. Use its recorded time. It does not establish the writer's identity or completed remediation. It is stored separately from certificate and proxy diagnostics. A missing file means no corresponding record is available; it does not mean the check passed. Successful actions do not establish that all threats were removed. remediation-case.json, when present, records the pre-remediation session and verification across boots or logons. It is a user-owned record, not administrator authorization, and its plans must not be replayed. Uncertain executions require checking protected results first. Recognized credential fields have been filtered, but records may still contain usernames, paths and command arguments. Review before sharing.

data.comment: Display-only key. Initial migration: SteamSentinel.Core/Reporting/ReportExporter.cs:186. Keep this key stable.

data.name: Report.ExportMarkdownAsync.79
data.value: File presence, runtime associations and Steam tampering are different kinds of evidence. The tool can quarantine known threats and offers heuristic actions requiring your review. Successful remediation does not establish that the whole computer is free of malware. Restart and rescan; use a professional antivirus for a full-disk scan if needed. If credential theft may have occurred, change passwords and revoke other sessions from a trusted device. Local restoration cannot recover data that has already leaked.

data.name: Ui.Xaml.MainWindow.116
data.value: Scanned media, scripts and executables are not run. Archive content is read in a separate process with Low Integrity and a restricted token. The process joins a dedicated Job Object before it receives scan paths and is terminated if its parent exits. Normal scanning does not request administrator privileges.
data.comment: Display only: MainWindow.xaml

data.name: Ui.Xaml.MainWindow.117
data.value: Remediation requires both a protected installation and intact components before administrator authorization. It requests UAC when needed; you can also open an administrator window and scan again while retaining the original window and report. Standard accounts need administrator credentials, which this tool does not collect. The administrator component checks the caller, plan SHA-256, exact paths, file hashes and directory pointers independently.
data.comment: Display only: MainWindow.xaml

data.name: Ui.Xaml.MainWindow.118
data.value: This tool focuses on Steam, Wallpaper Engine and observed fake-alert malware activity. After a quick scan, choose a full content scan following inspection, quarantine or Steam restoration. No known threat found does not mean the computer is absolutely safe. Password failures, unsupported formats, missing volumes or resource limits leave checks incomplete.
data.comment: Display only: MainWindow.xaml

data.name: Ui.Xaml.MainWindow.119
data.value: Heuristics provide review hints rather than certainty and are not selected by default. Successful remediation applies only to the targets in that plan; it does not certify the whole computer as malware-free. When needed, use maintained antimalware software for an independent full-disk review.
data.comment: Display only: MainWindow.xaml

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-WRAPPER-001.label
data.value: Confirmed malicious VPet plugin wrapper

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-WRAPPER-001.evidence
data.value: The exact original's LoadPlugin preserves the original plugin call, queues PxBridge.RunNear on the thread pool, and invokes the companion native loader. Based on read-only IL and component relationship verification on 2026-09-19.

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-CREDENTIAL-001.label
data.value: Confirmed Steam credential-stealing payload in VPet

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-CREDENTIAL-001.evidence
data.value: Static reconstruction of the exact original's data section revealed Steam memory/cache credential access, CryptUnprotectData, and upload code. Based on static analysis on 2026-09-19. A match does not establish execution or exfiltration.

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-LOADER-001.label
data.value: Confirmed malicious VPet native loader

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-LOADER-001.evidence
data.value: The exact original reconstructs the companion payload's data section through export ordinal 1 and manually maps its PE image. Based on disassembly and static data reconstruction on 2026-09-19; independent of component filenames.

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-STEAMUI-001.label
data.value: Confirmed Steam UI modification payload in VPet

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-STEAMUI-001.evidence
data.value: Static reconstruction of the exact original's data section revealed Steam support-route replacement, PX switches, and HTML/JS/CSS modification code. Based on static analysis on 2026-09-19; the payload was not executed.

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-ARCHIVE-001.label
data.value: VPet MOD archive containing confirmed malicious components

data.name: Rule.STEAMRED-VPET-ARCHIVE-001.evidence
data.value: The original ZIP statically verified on 2026-09-19 contains a malicious plugin wrapper, loader, Steam UI modification payload, and credential payload. An archive match establishes the presence of malicious content, not an infection on this computer. Legitimate dependencies and the original plugin are not classified as malicious merely because they share the archive.
